label: Window itself
summary: Gives the change-target window of a great holy war (GHW) as an object, so it can be passed on.
details: Going by its name, it hands over the window itself. The game does not use it with this window; the same name is used with other windows to pass them into helper functions.

label: Can confirm
summary: Whether the change of target in the great holy war target window can be confirmed.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of a button in this window. Going by its name, that is the confirm button; CanConfirmDesc is used as a tooltip in the same window.

label: Confirm tooltip
summary: A text for a tooltip in the great holy war target window, about confirming the change.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in this window. Going by its name, it explains whether or why the change can be confirmed.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the great holy war target window.
details: Vanilla runs it when a button in this window is clicked. It returns nothing.

label: Redirection cost
summary: The text of what it costs to change the target of a great holy war.
details: Vanilla puts it after the word "Cost:" in this window.

label: Cost tooltip
summary: The detailed text of the cost of changing a great holy war's target, for a tooltip.
details: Vanilla shows it under the heading "Redirection Cost", with the note that the cost rises every time the target is redirected.

label: Target titles
summary: The list of titles the window offers as the new target of the great holy war.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list that fills the window. Going by the entry type's name, each entry is one title item (ChangeGHWTargetWindowTitleItem). The game does not document the return type.

label: Has cost
summary: Whether changing the target costs something.
details: Going by its name and by the same function name on other interaction windows, where it controls whether a cost is shown. Vanilla does not use it on this window.

label: Confirm change
summary: Carries out the confirm action of the great holy war target window.
details: Vanilla runs it when the confirm button is clicked. It returns nothing.

label: Window itself
summary: The great holy war target window as an object.
details: Going by its name; the name appears very often with other types, where it passes the object itself into another function. The game does not use it with this window.

label: Item itself
summary: Gives one title entry of the great holy war target window as an object, so it can be passed on.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it with this type.

label: Defenders
summary: The list of defenders of the title that this entry stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list shown inside the entry. The game does not document the return type.

label: Title name
summary: The name text of this entry in the great holy war target window.
details: Going by its name and its text return type. The game does not use it with this type; GetTitle with GetNameNoTooltip is what vanilla uses.

label: Item size
summary: The size of this entry, as a pair of numbers (width and height).
details: Going by its name and return type. A same-named function on another title item is used to set a widget's size.

label: Title
summary: The title this entry stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the entry and then reads the title's name without tooltip from it.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether this title entry is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it for the pressed state of a widget (down) and for the visibility of another widget in the entry. Going by its name and the window, selected means chosen as the new target.

label: Select entry
summary: Runs what happens when this title entry is clicked.
details: Vanilla runs it on the entry's click. Going by IsSelected, the click chooses the entry. It returns nothing.

label: Item itself
summary: This title entry as an object.
details: Going by its name; the name appears very often with other types, where it passes the object itself into another function. The game does not use it with this type.

label: Access denied
summary: Whether the player may not access this character.
details: Vanilla uses it only together with debug mode, as Not(AccessDenied), to show extra widgets in the character and barbershop windows. The exact rule behind it is not documented.

label: Character itself
summary: Gives the character as an object, so it can be passed on.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it with a character. The same name is used with other widgets to pass them into helper functions.

label: Add to legend library
summary: A command that adds a legend to the character's legend library, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses the same name only as GetPlayer.AddToLegendLibrary( Legend.Self ) in the legend chronicle window, wrapped in PostCommand (do it), IsValidCommand (can it be done) and GetCommandDesc (tooltip). So it works as a command on the player's character.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The legend to add (vanilla passes a legend).

label: Adopt court language
summary: Makes the character's court use the given language.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click in the languages window, passing the language (a culture pillar) of the clicked entry. A variant named AdoptCourtLanguageNoPopup exists; going by that name, this one may show a popup. It returns nothing.

label: Adopt court language silently
summary: Makes the character's court use the given language, apparently without the popup.
details: Going by its name next to AdoptCourtLanguage; the game does not use it. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The language to adopt, going by AdoptCourtLanguage.

label: Titles destroyed on succession
summary: Whether all of the character's titles are destroyed when they die, instead of being passed on.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it.

label: Destiny scripted value
summary: Calculates a named script value for the character, with two other characters involved, and returns the number.
details: The one vanilla use is a test text: the value 'destiny_score_interest' with the player and the player's heir as the two extra arguments. Going by its name, it is meant for destiny scores.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the script value.
fields.values: a script value name in quotes

label: Script value
summary: Calculates a named script value with the character as its subject and returns the number.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts, for example 'character_difficulty_value' and 'medium_treasury_value', usually followed by |0 to show a whole number.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the script value.
fields.values: a script value name in quotes

label: Free consort slots
summary: The number of consort places the character could still fill.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it.

label: Free secondary spouse slots
summary: The number of secondary spouse places the character could still fill.
details: Vanilla passes it to GetNullCharacterDataModel in the character window. Going by that name, the number is used to make that many empty entries in a list.

label: Free spouse slots
summary: The number of spouse places the character could still fill.
details: Going by its name and the similar secondary spouse function; the game does not use it.

label: Grandeur from language
summary: How much court grandeur the character gets from using the given language at court.
details: Vanilla shows the number with a plus or minus sign as the baseline bonus in the court language texts, and shows the tooltip only when it is not zero.

label: Grandeur breakdown
summary: The parts that make up the court grandeur from the given language.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of a tooltip in the languages window. The game does not document the return type.

label: Can adopt court language
summary: Whether the character can make the given language their court language.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of the adopt buttons in the culture and languages windows.

label: Can afford cost
summary: Whether the character can pay the given cost.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it on a character. A same-named function on a building item is used to show a hint when the player cannot pay.

label: Can be acclaimed
summary: Whether the character can be acclaimed (given the acclaimed status of a knight).
details: Going by its name and the acclaimed knight texts; the game does not use it.

label: Can be punished
summary: Whether the character can be punished.
details: Vanilla uses it to control the visibility of widgets on character portraits. What exactly counts as punishable is not documented.

label: Can be renamed
summary: Whether the character can be renamed.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a rename button in the interaction menu, next to the data of a scripted GUI called rename_character_after_birth.

label: Can create legend
summary: Whether the character can create a legend from the given legend seed.
details: Vanilla uses it in the legends window as the enabled state of a widget, and its negation as the visibility of another.

label: Can create triggered legend
summary: Whether the character can create a legend from the given triggered legend seed.
details: Vanilla uses it in the legends window like CanCreateLegend, but with triggered legend seeds.

label: Can customize portrait
summary: Whether the character's portrait can be customized.
details: Vanilla uses it to control the visibility of widgets in the interaction menu, the barbershop and the character window.

label: Can design noble family
summary: Whether the character can have a noble family designed, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it in the multiplayer lobby, together with a selected playable character, as the enabled state of a widget.

label: Can have consorts
summary: Whether the character can have consorts.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it.

label: Can improve merit rank
summary: Whether the character can raise their merit rank.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it.

label: Can open decision
summary: Whether the character can open the given decision.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The decision, going by the name.

label: Can pick personal tenet
summary: Whether the character can choose the given tenet as a personal tenet.
details: Vanilla uses it in the personal beliefs window, for the add and swap buttons and their footer texts, together with a check that the tenet is not already personal. GetCannotPickAsPersonalTenetReason gives the reason when not.

label: Player can change focus
summary: Whether the player may change this character's focus.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it.

label: Can raid
summary: Whether the character is able to raid.
details: Vanilla uses it to control the visibility of widgets in the military window.

label: Can send interaction
summary: Whether the character can send the given character interaction.
details: Vanilla uses it with the interaction 'transfer_small_gold_amount_to_treasury_interaction' to enable a button in the HUD.

label: Can start bartering
summary: Whether the character can start bartering.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it.

label: Can start raid
summary: Whether the character can start a raid right now.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it. Vanilla uses CanRaid instead.

label: Knows of killer
summary: Whether the character knows who killed the given character.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character who was killed, going by the name.

label: Copy DNA
summary: Copies the character's DNA, going by its name, probably to the clipboard.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button in the character window that is shown in debug mode. It returns nothing.

label: Copy persistent DNA
summary: Copies the character's persistent DNA, going by its name, probably to the clipboard.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button in the character window. The difference to the plain DNA copy is not documented. It returns nothing.

label: Copy accessory DNA
summary: Copies the DNA of the character's accessory to the clipboard, going by its name.
details: Vanilla runs it from buttons in the barbershop and in a shared tooltip. It returns nothing.

label: Copy portrait animation
summary: Copies the character's portrait animation to the clipboard, going by its name.
details: Vanilla runs it from buttons in the barbershop and in a shared tooltip. It returns nothing.

label: Courtier wants to leave
summary: Whether the courtier wants to leave the court.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it.

label: Custom text
summary: Runs a custom localization with the character as its subject and returns the text.
details: The most common call in the game's texts, for example Character.Custom('CharacterDifficulty'). The name is the key of a custom localization entry.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the custom localization.
fields.values: a custom localization key in quotes

label: Custom text with one more
summary: Runs a custom localization with the character as its subject and one extra value, and returns the text.
details: Vanilla passes another subject as the second argument, for example a character or a title, which the custom text then uses.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the custom localization.
fields.values: a custom localization key in quotes

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The extra value handed to the custom text.
fields.values: a character, title or similar object

label: Custom text with flag
summary: Like Custom2, but the extra value is a flag name.
details: Vanilla uses it in artifact descriptions with SCOPE.GetFlagName('...') as the second argument, for example the metal or gem type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the custom localization.
fields.values: a custom localization key in quotes

fields.name: Arg1
fields.values: a flag name, for example from GetFlagName

label: Custom text with title
summary: Like Custom2, but the extra value is a title.
details: Vanilla uses it in stele descriptions with a saved title (sTitle) as the second argument.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the custom localization.
fields.values: a custom localization key in quotes

label: Custom text, fixed random
summary: Runs a custom localization with the character as its subject and returns the text.
details: Going by its name, the random choice inside the custom text stays the same each time it is shown. Vanilla uses it for synonyms and animal names in event texts.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the custom localization.
fields.values: a custom localization key in quotes

label: Employs court position
summary: Whether the character has someone in the given type of court position.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The court position type, going by the name.

label: Employs court positions
summary: Whether the character employs court positions, going by its name.
details: The game does not use it.

label: AI boldness
summary: The character's boldness value used by the AI, a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in a debug tooltip listing the AI values (honor, greed, rationality, energy, boldness and so on).

label: AI boldness with dread
summary: The character's AI boldness after the player's dread (fear) is taken into account, a number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the debug tooltip as "Dread Modified Boldness", right after plain boldness.

label: AI compassion
summary: The character's compassion value used by the AI, a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the debug tooltip listing the AI values.

label: AI energy
summary: The character's energy value used by the AI, a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the debug tooltip listing the AI values.

label: AI greed
summary: The character's greed value used by the AI, a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the debug tooltip listing the AI values.

label: AI honor
summary: The character's honor value used by the AI, a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the debug tooltip listing the AI values.

label: AI personality
summary: The text name of the character's AI personality.
details: Vanilla shows it in a personality summary tooltip and as raw text in the court position window.

label: AI personality explanation
summary: A text explaining the character's AI personality.
details: Vanilla uses it as a text in the shared tooltip.

label: AI personality, no tooltip
summary: The text name of the character's AI personality, without a tooltip on it.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character window and in the shared tooltip.

label: AI rationality
summary: The character's rationality value used by the AI, a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the debug tooltip listing the AI values.

label: AI sociability
summary: The character's sociability value used by the AI, a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the debug tooltip listing the AI values.

label: AI vengefulness
summary: The character's vengefulness value used by the AI, a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the debug tooltip listing the AI values.

label: AI zeal
summary: The character's zeal value used by the AI, a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the debug tooltip listing the AI values.

label: Accepted task contracts
summary: The list of task contracts the character has accepted.
details: Vanilla uses it on the player in the HUD as the list to show. The game does not document the return type.

label: Acclaimed accolade
summary: The accolade of the character as an acclaimed knight.
details: Vanilla reads its name in the acclaimed knight relation text and checks IsValid on it in the army window, so it can be empty when the character has none. The game does not document the return type.

label: Accolades
summary: The list of accolades of the character.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list in the knights window. The game does not document the return type.

label: Active council task
summary: The council task the character is currently doing.
details: Going by its name; the same name is used on a council task interaction item in the GUI. The game does not document the return type.

label: Active law with flag
summary: The law the character's realm currently has in the law group marked with the given flag.
details: Vanilla uses it with 'succession_order_laws' and then reads the law's name, to show the realm's succession law. The game does not document the return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The flag of the law group.
fields.values: a law group flag in quotes

label: Activity state text
summary: A text describing the state of the activity the character is in.
details: Vanilla passes 'short' to get the short form, for example in the activity list window.

label: Court language cost
summary: The text of what it costs the character to adopt a new court language.
details: Vanilla shows it in the court language info text, which also says how long they must wait before adopting another.

label: Age
summary: The character's age in years, a whole number.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character window's age texts and many other texts.

label: Age info
summary: A short text about the character's age.
details: Vanilla puts it after the death date of a dead character, before the birth date. The exact wording is the game's.

label: AI budget description
summary: A text describing the character's AI budget.
details: Vanilla shows it in the debug tooltip with the AI values.

label: Animated portrait
summary: An animated portrait picture of the character, for a portrait widget.
details: Vanilla gives it four arguments: the environment, the camera, the animation (for example 'idle') and the widget's screen size. A variant named GetAnimatedPortraitEvenIfDead exists; going by that name, this one may not show dead characters.

label: Animated portrait, also dead
summary: An animated portrait picture of the character, also when the character is dead.
details: Takes the same four arguments as GetAnimatedPortrait. Going by its name, the plain version leaves out dead characters.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.values: an animation name, or a legend's portrait animation

label: Animation name
summary: The name of the animation the character's portrait is playing.
details: Vanilla shows it in quotes followed by the word "Animation" in the portrait modifier texts.

label: Appointment timeout text
summary: A text about the time left before the character can be appointed again.
details: Vanilla shows it in tooltips next to the date when the new appointment cooldown ends.

label: Approval reasons
summary: A text listing the reasons behind the character's approval.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it.

label: Assigned tax slot
summary: The tax slot (tax jurisdiction) assigned to the character.
details: Vanilla reads its name after the label "Tax Jurisdiction". The game does not document the return type.

label: Average development
summary: The character's average development level, a number.
details: Going by its name; vanilla shows it in the ledger as a whole number. What it averages over is not documented.

label: Powerful vassals' expectation
summary: The average legitimacy that the character's powerful vassals expect of them.
details: Vanilla uses it in the average expectations tooltip next to the legitimacy type. The game does not document the return type.

label: Vassals' expectation
summary: The average legitimacy that the character's vassals expect of them.
details: Vanilla uses it in the average expectations tooltip, next to the powerful vassals' figure. The game does not document the return type.

label: Away courtiers
summary: The list of the character's courtiers who are away.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it.

label: Balance
summary: The character's income balance, a number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger with the sign and one decimal.

label: Balance breakdown
summary: A text showing what makes up the character's balance.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger.

label: Theocratic lease balance
summary: The gold per month the character gets from their theocratic lease, a number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the church property tooltip of the character window with a gold icon, per month, under the taxes line, after the number of temples under the lease.

label: Banish reasons
summary: A text listing the reasons the character can or cannot be banished, for the given character.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: A character, going by the name (probably who banishes).

label: Barter goods tooltip
summary: A tooltip text about the character's barter goods and their balance.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the character window.

label: Base weight
summary: The character's base body weight, a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the character debug tooltip as "Base Weight", next to target weight and current weight.

label: Beneficiary
summary: The beneficiary of a great holy war, as a character.
details: Vanilla shows its name in the great holy war window and checks IsValid on it, so it can be empty. Who is the beneficiary is not documented here.

label: Betrothed
summary: The character the character is betrothed to.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it.

label: Birth date
summary: The date the character was born.
details: Vanilla reads its text form (GetString) in the tooltip of a dead character.

label: Court language reason
summary: A text saying whether and why the character can adopt the given court language.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the languages window and in the culture window text.

label: Cost tooltip text
summary: A text saying whether the character can afford the given cost.
details: Going by its name and its match with CanAffordCost; the game does not use it.

label: Create legend reason
summary: A text saying whether and why the character can create a legend from the given seed.
details: Vanilla adds it as a line to the create legend tooltip.

label: Create triggered legend reason
summary: A text saying whether and why the character can create a legend from the given triggered seed.
details: Vanilla uses it in the create triggered legend tooltip.

label: Why not personal tenet
summary: A text giving the reason the character cannot pick the given tenet as a personal tenet.
details: Vanilla uses it in the personal beliefs window together with CanPickAsPersonalTenet.

label: Capital location
summary: The place of the character's capital.
details: Vanilla reads from it, for example its terrain name, in culture title texts and in travel tooltips. The game does not document the return type; what kind of place it is (county or province) is not stated.

label: Career path text
summary: A text describing the character's career path.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the HUD.

label: Challenger
summary: The character's challenger.
details: Vanilla checks IsValid on the player's challenger in the inventory window, so it can be empty. The game does not document the return type.

label: Challenger sponsor
summary: The sponsor of the character's challenger.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it.

label: Challenger sponsor title
summary: The title belonging to the challenger's sponsor.
details: Going by its name; the game does not use it.

label: Employed as
summary: The character who holds the given court position for this character.
details: Vanilla uses it with 'antiquarian_court_position' in the inventory window. The game does not document the return type; the use suggests an employed character.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a court position key in quotes

label: Name, view style
summary: The character's name as the character window shows it.
